# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (first of the run; empty seed)

- **Strategy tried:** an empty seed is not "iteration 1 of a hill climb", it is a cold start, so I
  did not hunt for one big lever. I clustered **all 22** failures first, then shipped one edit per
  cluster with a different lever type each (CONTRACT, STRUCTURE-ordering, STRUCTURE-code,
  DECISION-rule, KNOWLEDGE-fact, KNOWLEDGE-idiom). No LEDGER rows exist yet to cite.
- **The process step that paid off most was cheap and non-obvious: reading the adapter read-only
  before writing a word of prose.** It revealed that an *empty* `prompt.md` means "no system
  message" (not a default), that the built-in template carries the "file exists ⇒ done" line, that
  only the first code block is executed, and that the preview is `header=0`. Four of the eight
  shipped edits exist only because of that read. Recommend every cold-start iteration do this first.
- **Counting beat reasoning.** Two tallies decided the candidate's shape: formula-writers 0/13 vs
  literal-writers 18/27, and 39-of-40 never-verified. Both took minutes to compute from the traces
  and are far stronger evidence than reading any single trace closely. Cheap aggregate counts over
  all trajectories, before deep-reading any of them.
- **The highest-value process step was regression-testing my own prose as code.** The audit snippet
  is the only edit that tells the agent to go back and change a file it may already have written
  correctly — so I extracted it verbatim from the written file and *ran* it against real workbooks
  for 13 tasks (8 passing, 5 failing). That found **two real bugs I would otherwise have shipped**:
  unbounded printing (1280 lines), and a classifier that swept legitimately-blank cells into
  `MUST-FIX`, false-alarming on exactly the 5 fragile passing tasks. **Generalizable rule: if a
  prompt edit contains executable code, execute it against gold before shipping — do not review it
  by reading.**
- **A self-audit against gold caught an over-strong rule.** I had written "empty is never an answer";
  checking gold blankness across the 18 passing tasks showed 5 of them have legitimately blank gold
  (382-10 is 79% blank). The SAFE test is much sharper when run as a *query against the passing
  tasks' gold* than as introspection about blast radius.
- **Subagents:** read-only `Explore` agents per trajectory group for clustering, merged into one
  candidate. Useful for breadth. One of my own hypotheses was refuted by a subagent's evidence,
  which changed shipped wording — so state hypotheses explicitly in the delegation prompt and ask
  for disconfirmation, not confirmation.
- **Plateau signal:** none possible yet.
- **What to try next iteration:** (a) read cand_0001's RESULT before anything else — with 8 edits
  shipped together, a rejection will not say which one hurt, so if it regresses, bisect by lever
  (drop the audit snippet first; it has the largest behavioural blast radius) rather than rewriting.
  (b) If it lands, the remaining mass is *semantic* misreading of the instruction (unit of
  aggregation, which row set) — a different lever class from anything shipped here, which was all
  contract/mechanics. (c) Keep the "run the prose" discipline; it is the only step this iteration
  that found defects nothing else would have.
- **Cost note for the run:** the breadth-first approach used one iteration to cover 8 clusters. If
  the RESULT is a clean accept, prefer breadth again; if it is a rejection with a small `broke={}`
  set, the run will have paid a whole iteration to learn one bad edit — in that case switch to
  2–3 edits per iteration so attribution is possible.

<!-- cap-evolve:meta-insights-append-below -->

## Iteration cand_0003 (run so far: ACCEPT +0.450, then reject +0.000 — val flat at 0.900)

- **cand_0001's own cost note predicted cand_0002's failure, and was not acted on.** It wrote: *"if
  it is a rejection with a small `broke={}` set, the run will have paid a whole iteration to learn
  one bad edit — in that case switch to 2–3 edits per iteration so attribution is possible."*
  cand_0002 then shipped **6** edits, was rejected with `broke={2768, 51-12}`, and the framework
  reverted **all six** — including the two that demonstrably *fixed* 227-40 and 267-18. The run paid
  a full iteration and recovered zero of the win. **The meta-lesson is not "batch smaller" in the
  abstract — it is that under a revert-the-whole-batch gate, one bad edit has unbounded cost, so the
  per-edit blast-radius check is worth more than an extra fix.** A forecast written in META_INSIGHTS
  is worthless unless the next iteration reads it as a rule; I am restating it as one here.
- **Strategy tried this iteration: same diagnoses, narrower gates.** With val flat at 0.900 for two
  iterations and only 4 tasks (~0.10) of headroom left — *less than the gate's own resolvable effect
  size, 2·SE = 0.1013* — a batch that fixes 2 and breaks 2 mathematically cannot clear the bar. So
  the search problem has changed shape: it is no longer "find more fixes", it is **"make each fix
  unable to reach a passing task"**. Every clause I shipped is conditioned, and the one edit I could
  not bound was chosen to be *write-neutral* (it adds a check, never a write). Whether this is the
  right lever is exactly what this iteration's RESULT will measure.
- **The process step that paid off most: deriving the breakage MECHANISM from traces, not guessing
  from the `broke` list.** `broke={2768, 51-12}` alone would have supported a dozen theories. Ten
  minutes of grepping gave a named mechanism for each — 2768's answer range is *fully pre-filled* and
  its gold overwrites all 17 cells (so the "preserve pre-filled" clause is lethal there); 51-12 is
  the *longest trajectory in the set* at 10 rounds vs 4 for 31/40 (so it is the task least able to
  absorb a new mandatory step, and its logic hinges on a numeric comparison the new operator table
  invited re-litigating). **Generalizable: before redesigning an edit, find the sentence in the
  broken task's own trace or preview that the edit would have changed.** If you cannot, you are
  guessing.
- **Aggregate counting paid off again, and is now the cheapest tool in this run.** Three counts
  decided three gates: 40-preview scans for demo/expected wording (4 hits, 3 excluded by the gate)
  and for created/closed wording (**1** hit); and `COUNTS:` lines across passing Cell-Level tasks
  (all zero-BLANK ⇒ "near-empty coverage" is a trigger that *cannot* fire on a passing task). Each
  took one command and converted a hand-wave about blast radius into a number.
- **Verification degraded and the method had to adapt.** cand_0002 executed its edits against the
  benchmark gold workbooks; those are unreachable from this sandbox. Substitute ladder that worked:
  execute against a **synthetic workbook reproducing the structure** (proved the input-formula
  erasure and the datetime mis-classification outright), then **directional** reasoning from the
  scorer's feedback string (a strictly-more-permissive predicate can only inflate a count — matching
  "HIGHER than expected"), then **counting** the demo block against the scorer's stated expected-cell
  count (17 = 17). Recommend this ladder to any iteration that cannot reach gold; it is weaker than
  gold execution but much stronger than reading.
- **Plateau signal: yes, two flat iterations.** Lever switched: (a) gating over breadth, as above;
  (b) from **type-level** to **semantic** verification — cand_0001 bought +0.450 with a type-level
  audit, and 43436 proves that level is exhausted (`MUST-FIX: []` on five wrong numbers). Every
  remaining failure passes the type audit, so the audit had to grow a semantics obligation or stop
  being the lever.
- **Subagents: none** (session config forbids them unless requested). Cost: the 40-trace sweep was
  serial. It was affordable because the counts above are one-command aggregates; a breadth-first
  *reading* pass would not have been.
- **What to try next iteration (4 of 5; 1 reject so far, budget is tight):**
  1. **Read the RESULT before anything else.** If Δ≈0 again with fixed≈broke, gating has failed as a
     strategy — then ship **exactly one** edit (edit 1: narrowest, best-verified, executed against a
     synthetic twin) to buy a clean single-variable measurement. With one or two iterations left, a
     confirmed +1 task beats another unattributable batch.
  2. If the RESULT accepts, **do not immediately re-batch.** Re-introduce the skipped cand_0002
     `ERASED` check alone, since it is the last untried edit with a real mechanism behind it.
  3. If a *new* task regresses, suspect a **gate that fired too widely** before suspecting the fix it
     guards — that is the failure mode this iteration's design newly introduces.
  4. Standing rule for this run: **never ship a clause that tells the agent what to preserve.** Two
     of the three regressions-worth-of-evidence so far trace to preservation language, and the
     benchmark routinely asks for pre-filled cells to be overwritten.
